title: Peregrine Systems - marketplace listing & packaging + reference architecture review
transcript_header: Date: 2026-07-21 | Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 1h14m | Recording: yes. Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood SE), Devon Brooks (Redwood Solutions), Arman Raja (Peregrine Cloud Architect), Priya Desai (Peregrine Partnerships), Evan McAllister (Peregrine Platform), Sonia Gupta (Peregrine Security).
summary: Workshop to align on AWS/GCP marketplace packaging approach, reference architecture for a hybrid deployment (hosted + on-prem connector), and checklist for Peregrine's listing certification. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share helm chart and container manifest, Peregrine to provide security questionnaire answers and billing metering dimensions, schedule pilot benchmark week. Discussed KMS/HSM, SSO, private offers, marketplace tile requirements, and automation for EKS/ECS/GKE installs.
topics: Marketplace packaging options (SaaS listing vs container/AMI/Helm)
Reference architecture for hybrid deployments (VPC peering, private link, on-prem connector)
Security artifacts required (SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs)
Billing / metering model and private offer flow
Deployment automation and CI for marketplace images
action_items: Maya Ortiz: Export trimmed helm chart + deployment manifest and upload to shared repo (due 2026-07-28)
Peregrine - Evan McAllister: Provide container image size, supported architectures (x86/ARM) and OCI repo access (due 2026-07-26)
Sonia Gupta: Fill and send back Redwood's security questionnaire (due 2026-07-30)
Liam Chen: Draft suggested SaaS metering dimension and sample invoice line items for marketplace (due 2026-07-24)
All: Schedule 1-week pilot benchmark slot (proposed 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-14) pending image access
next_steps: Redwood to share a packaged reference arch diagram (PNG + Visio) and a short install playbook
Peregrine to confirm whether they want a SaaS Marketplace listing or a container/Helm listing (decision by 2026-07-26)
Set up GitHub repo with helm chart and CI pipeline examples (Redwood will create initial skeleton)
Book follow-up call after Peregrine returns security artifacts to run marketplace compliance checklist
transcript:
[00:00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — let's do quick intros and then dive into the packaging options. Uh, goal for today is to converge on 1) marketplace listing type, 2) what we need to deliver for listing cert, and 3) reference arch for Peregrine's hybrid deployment.

[00:00:18] Priya Desai: Thanks Liam, from our side Priya here, I'm running partnerships and we'll own the listing side. Arman is our cloud architect and Evan runs the platform. Sonia is on for security.

[00:00:30] Maya Ortiz: Hi all, Maya, I'm Redwood SE; I'll go through install/manifest and ops concerns. Devon will jump in for solutions questions.

[00:00:42] Arman Raja: Quick context — Peregrine currently runs a multi-tenant control plane in our VPC on AWS, some of our customers run us in their own VPC or on-prem via a lightweight connector. For marketplace, priority is to shorten buyer deploy time and keep security controls intact.

[00:01:05] Liam Chen: Great. First big decision: SaaS listing (hosted by Peregrine / Redwood SaaS integration) vs packaged listing (container/Helm/AMI). Each has pros/cons. SaaS = easier billing, Redwood can route traffic to dedicated pools; packaged is more flexible for air-gapped customers. Thoughts?

[00:01:30] Evan McAllister: We're leaning packaged + helm chart because a chunk of our enterprise customers require us to run in their VPC. But we also want a SaaS option, maybe start with packaged and later add a SaaS tile.

[00:01:45] Maya Ortiz: Makes sense. For Helm we need to confirm: manifests, values.yaml, post-install hooks for licensing, and images. Also whether you want an operator or just plain helm. Operator increases complexity for marketplace certs.

[00:02:03] Sonia Gupta: On security — we'll need to submit SOC2 report, encryption-at-rest proof (KMS or customer-managed keys), SAML SSO integration docs, and audit logging. Also need clarity on where logs and telemetry go for packaged installs.

[00:02:21] Liam Chen: Right, Redwood's experience: marketplace packaging teams will ask for a clear data flow diagram, encryption key model, and a way to produce tenant-level audit logs. For hosted we offer KMS integration and bring-your-own-key via HSM—customer-managed KMS for dedicated deployments.

[00:02:40] Arman Raja: For the on-prem connector we use a small sidecar process that tunnels over a TLS connection out to our control plane. We'll need to show that topology in the ref arch. Question: can Redwood's runtime be deployed as a local inference enclave or only in our cloud?

[00:02:58] Maya Ortiz: Redwood runtime supports both: hosted inference and dedicated private deployment. For packaged we can provide a container image that runs the lightweight runtime; for on-prem we have an installer that can run in air-gapped mode but that requires additional licensing and verified images.

[00:03:20] Devon Brooks: Small note — when you package the image, make sure layers are minimized; marketplace scanners will flag >10GB images, and that impacts private customers with slow registries. Also, include multi-arch manifests if you want ARM support.

[00:03:37] Evan McAllister: Got it. We'll check image sizes. We recently built an ARM build for edge nodes.

[00:03:45] Priya Desai: Pricing/metering question — if we go packaged, how does billing work? We want marketplace to handle purchase flow.

[00:03:53] Liam Chen: For packaged software there's usually a private offer or marketplace transactable listing with license-based billing. For SaaS, usage metering is native — Redwood can help propose a metering dimension (e.g., inference units per 1k tokens or per concurrent seat). I'll draft a sample invoice mapping.

[00:04:12] Maya Ortiz: Important to align on metering early: some marketplaces require exact dimension names and numeric ranges; also SKU per region if you plan multi-region pricing.

[00:04:25] Arman Raja: Another constraint: some accounts require VPC endpoints only; they don't allow public egress. For the connector, we need a variant that supports reverse-VPN or private link to maintain no public egress.

[00:04:40] Sonia Gupta: That ties into KMS — we need to ensure keys never leave customer environment if required. For SaaS, we need to document KMS options and whether bring-your-own-key is supported.

[00:04:52] Liam Chen: Redwood supports BYOK for Dedicated and Private; hosted can support customer-managed keys with a few extra steps. We'll capture that in the security artifact pack.

[00:05:04] Maya Ortiz: Technical deep dive — here's what the reference arch should show: ingress options (ALB vs NLB), VPC peering or PrivateLink, connector architecture for on-prem, and placement of the KV cache for inference (local vs shared). Also show fallback to cheaper model variant if capacity hit.

[00:05:30] Arman Raja: On KV cache — we prefer local cache on the inference pod to reduce cross-VPC latency. Is that supported in Redwood runtime?

[00:05:38] Maya Ortiz: Yes, the runtime supports local KV caching and distributed cache via Redis. For packaged installs we recommend local KV plus optional Redis for multi-node scenarios.

[00:05:48] Evan McAllister: Performance question — we'll want a smoke benchmark that simulates our typical seq length distribution; can Redwood help run that once we give the image?

[00:05:57] Liam Chen: Absolutely. Next step we can do a 1-week benchmark. We'll need a sample prompt set, target latency SLOs, and expected tokens per request. We'll run hosted and dedicated scenarios if you want.

[00:06:10] Priya Desai: On the listing tile — what assets are required? screenshots, short video, logos, architecture diagram?

[00:06:17] Maya Ortiz: Marketplace typically wants 1) product summary, 2) hero image, 3) 1-2 screenshots or deployment flow, 4) architecture diagram, 5) support contact, 6) pricing tiers and metering definition. We'll attach a template in the docs.

[00:06:33] Liam Chen: Also confirm if you want private offers — private offers allow direct contract negotiation and custom pricing, useful for enterprise deals.

[00:06:40] Priya Desai: Yes private offers are key for us. We want to control discounting and term negotiation.

[00:06:45] Sonia Gupta: Compliance flow — who signs the DPA and how is data residency captured on the listing? We need explicit regions and data flow statements.

[00:06:53] Liam Chen: We'll include a data residency statement in the listing and a DPA example. For Dedicated/Private we can specify region constraints; the listing can include region availability text.

[00:07:05] Arman Raja: Quick improv — for on-prem installs we also need to support offline registries; is Redwood's installer friendly for air-gapped environments?

[00:07:12] Maya Ortiz: Yes but with caveats: you need to pre-pull images and provide licensing tokens. We have an air-gap installer flow and a signing step for images. We'll share the flow doc.

[00:07:20] Devon Brooks: Another small gotcha — marketplace certification teams sometimes reject manifests with execStart hooks that call out to external URLs. Keep post-install network calls optional and documented.

[00:07:33] Evan McAllister: Noted. We'll ensure no mandatory external calls during install.

[00:07:40] Priya Desai: Can Redwood host the initial SaaS tile while we finish packaged work? Like a joint offering where Redwood hosts inference for early customers?

[00:07:48] Liam Chen: We can discuss a limited hosted pilot under Redwood's hosted API or Dedicated reserved capacity. We have an onboarding accelerator for partner pilots. Cost and SLA would be discussed in the follow-up.

[00:07:59] Sonia Gupta: For the security questionnaire: where do we upload? Is there a secure intake?

[00:08:04] Liam Chen: We'll provide an SFTP link and a secure intake form; I'll attach it to the follow-up email.

[00:08:10] Maya Ortiz: I'm going to screen-share a quick checklist I use for marketplace packaging — (small screen-share noises) — checklist items: manifest cleanliness, probe configs, resource requests, RBAC least privilege, docker labels, image signing, helm chart values, and a simple smoke test.

[00:08:38] (screen-share) Maya Ortiz: Okay, first item: manifests. Try to keep CRDs minimal. If you use an operator, include a CRD migration note.

[00:08:50] Arman Raja: We're using a small CRD set for multi-tenant routing; we'll document migration steps.

[00:08:57] Devon Brooks: On telemetry — include an option to forward metrics to a customer-managed endpoint or to a SaaS ingestion endpoint. Customers vary.

[00:09:07] Evan McAllister: We prefer a customer-managed metrics option; we use Prometheus and Grafana.

[00:09:12] Maya Ortiz: Good. Also include a minimal smoke test that users can run post-install: health endpoint, sample inference request with a short model and token counts, and a connectivity check to KMS if using BYOK.

[00:09:26] Priya Desai: Anything else re: legal / procurement for marketplace?

[00:09:31] Liam Chen: Marketplace procurement usually requires evidence of support SLAs, a simple T&C / EULA text, and contact for support. We'll provide a template EULA and a partner support matrix.

[00:09:45] Sonia Gupta: We'll need to see a redacted DPA and SOC2. Also whether Redwood can provide attestations around runtime isolation.

[00:09:53] Liam Chen: We'll include those artifacts. We can share a redacted SOC2 report and a runtime isolation write-up.

[00:10:02] Arman Raja: On the ref arch diagram — include ports, CIDR blocks examples (not real IPs), and sequence flows for onboarding, normal inference, and failover.

[00:10:12] Maya Ortiz: Agreed. We'll produce a diagram template showing ALB/NLB, NAT vs no-NAT patterns, PrivateLink and a connector reverse tunnel variant.

[00:10:23] Devon Brooks: I also recommend a scripted installer for enterprises that want zero-touch via cloud-init or similar. Helm is great, but a CLI wrapper helps.

[00:10:32] Evan McAllister: We can add a small wrapper. We'll coordinate with Devon on CLI options.

[00:10:38] Liam Chen: Timeline — if Peregrine can provide images and security artifacts this week, Redwood can produce the helm skeleton, diagram, and a sample metering proposal by next Friday. Then aim for pilot in mid-August. Is that realistic?

[00:10:52] Priya Desai: Sounds good, we just need to align internal approvals.

[00:10:58] Sonia Gupta: I'll prioritize the security questionnaire.

[00:11:02] Maya Ortiz: I'll add to the shared repo a checklist and a sample smoke test harness (simple python scripts).

[00:11:09] (minor cross-talk)

[00:11:15] Liam Chen: Ok let's call out the concrete next steps — we've captured them in the action items. Anything else?

[00:11:22] Arman Raja: One last question — any gotchas around marketplace metadata size limits? Some require short descriptions under 400 characters.

[00:11:29] Maya Ortiz: Yes, keep the hero blurb tight and use bullet points for features. We'll share a copy deck with character limits.

[00:11:37] Priya Desai: Great. If there's nothing else we'll wrap. Thanks everyone.

[00:11:43] Liam Chen: Thanks all — I'll send the follow-up with the SFTP link, the checklist, and draft metering proposal. We'll reconvene once Peregrine returns the security pack.

[00:11:53] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions and overlapping speech. Some technical terms abbreviated (KV cache, BYOK, CRD) and the team used shorthand. There were a few inaudible segments around minute marks 00:07:00-00:07:12 due to screen-share noises.
